Climate, measured independently of light. Each unit's share of the five UNEP aridity classes from the Global Aridity Index v3.1, on true cell areas rather than pixel counts. This is what the light-derived exclusion scopes are checked against in [`../docs/aridity.md`](../docs/aridity.md).

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `iso3` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code |
| `gid` | GADM identifier of the province |
| `name` | GADM name of the province |
| `area_km2` | unit area on the WGS 84 ellipsoid |
| `pixels_total` | aridity cells falling in the unit |
| `pixels_classified` | cells carrying a real aridity value; the rest are ocean or permanent ice, and are excluded from every share below |
| `pixels_unclassified` | `pixels_total` − `pixels_classified` |
| `hyper_arid_share` | area share with aridity index < 0.03 |
| `arid_share` | 0.03 ≤ AI < 0.20 |
| `semi_arid_share` | 0.20 ≤ AI < 0.50 |
| `dry_subhumid_share` | 0.50 ≤ AI < 0.65 |
| `humid_share` | AI ≥ 0.65 |
| `desert_share` | `hyper_arid_share` + `arid_share` — the UNEP definition of desert |
| `dryland_share` | everything below AI 0.65, i.e. 1 − `humid_share` |
| `level` | admin level the row describes; always `adm1` here |

`sha256:3168ab2fa794ce93a9d6a179c0a547b33d090c847bc9d5c904ddfaa2a7ac69e6`

## Netherlands: province zonal table

[`NLD/NLD_adm1_zonal.csv`](NLD/NLD_adm1_zonal.csv) — 434 rows

Per-province aggregation, the basis of every subnational number above. Each land pixel belongs to exactly one unit, so `sum_of_lights` totals to the national figure for every year.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `year` | calendar year, 1992–2022 |
| `gid` | GADM `GID_1` code — stable across releases, unlike names |
| `name` | GADM `NAME_1` |
| `pixels` | land pixels assigned to the unit |
| `area_km2` | unit area from the GADM geometry, in EPSG:8857 |
| `sum_of_lights` | Σ DN over the unit's pixels |
| `mean_dn` | `sum_of_lights` ÷ `pixels` |
| `density_sol_per_km2` | `sum_of_lights` ÷ `area_km2` — the quantity the subnational Gini and Theil are computed over |

`sha256:a1b5dc16873d01a77e6a5ca5a4da5484b34c98ad79f20fd647880376375afe6b`

## Netherlands: municipality zonal table

[`NLD/NLD_adm2_zonal.csv`](NLD/NLD_adm2_zonal.csv) — 11,005 rows

Per-municipality aggregation, the basis of every subnational number above. Each land pixel belongs to exactly one unit, so `sum_of_lights` totals to the national figure for every year. **Check `pixels` before trusting a density**: the smallest units cover only a pixel or two, so their densities are extremely noisy. They are kept rather than dropped silently, so the choice is yours and visible.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `year` | calendar year, 1992–2022 |
| `gid` | GADM `GID_2` code — stable across releases, unlike names |
| `name` | GADM `NAME_2` |
| `pixels` | land pixels assigned to the unit |
| `area_km2` | unit area from the GADM geometry, in EPSG:8857 |
| `sum_of_lights` | Σ DN over the unit's pixels |
| `mean_dn` | `sum_of_lights` ÷ `pixels` |
| `density_sol_per_km2` | `sum_of_lights` ÷ `area_km2` — the quantity the subnational Gini and Theil are computed over |

`sha256:599346306435abac5c6756fc1ccd83020e80b325dc24760b864ae5bc2c27ea1e`

## North Macedonia: inequality series

[`MKD/MKD_inequality_series.csv`](MKD/MKD_inequality_series.csv) — 93 rows

The headline result. Pixel-level rows are the distribution of DN over land pixels; subnational rows are the distribution of **light density** (SOL/km²) over units, unweighted, so a large unit does not score high merely for being large.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `year` | calendar year, 1992–2022 |
| `level` | `pixel`, `adm1` (municipality) |
| `level_label` | human-readable form of `level` |
| `scope` | unit set — `all` (every unit) |
| `zeros` | pixel zero treatment: `zeros_included` (all land pixels) or `lit_only` (DN > 0). Blank for subnational rows, where the unit is the observation |
| `n` | observations behind the index: pixels, or units |
| `gini` | Gini coefficient; `nan` if the distribution is all-zero |
| `theil_t` | Theil T = GE(1); maximum is ln(n) |
| `theil_l` | Theil L = GE(0); `nan` whenever any value is 0, since ln(μ/x) diverges — which is why the zeros-included pixel rows are undefined rather than large |
| `sum_of_lights` | total DN over the scope, for reference |
| `lit_share` | fraction of land pixels with DN > 0; pixel rows only |

`sha256:6800adfa81f627523b4442bb7a306012ac936a05badaedb6bd3b205af573027e`

## North Macedonia: Theil decomposition

[`MKD/MKD_theil_decomposition.csv`](MKD/MKD_theil_decomposition.csv) — 124 rows

Additive between/within splits of pixel-level Theil. `residual` is the identity check: it stays at machine precision on every defined row, so the split is exact rather than approximate.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `year` | calendar year, 1992–2022 |
| `scope` | unit set — `all` (every unit) |
| `zeros` | pixel zero treatment: `zeros_included` (all land pixels) or `lit_only` (DN > 0). Blank for subnational rows, where the unit is the observation |
| `measure` | `theil_t` or `theil_l` |
| `grouping` | `municipality` only; GADM has no admin-2 layer for this country, so there is no `nested` row |
| `total` | the index over all pixels in scope |
| `between` | between-group component |
| `within` | within-group component |
| `between_share` | `between` ÷ `total` |
| `within_share` | `within` ÷ `total` |
| `between_deleg_within_gov` | the middle term of the nested split: variation between admin-2 units of the same admin-1 unit. `nan` otherwise |
| `residual` | |total − (between + within)|; a correctness check |
| `n_groups` | groups with at least one pixel in scope |

`sha256:48711b8020bde2a5463e73d68ad9a79da91f13d7b6019295e32badaf3448014b`

## North Macedonia: per-unit Theil contributions

[`MKD/MKD_theil_by_unit.csv`](MKD/MKD_theil_by_unit.csv) — 5,015 rows

What each unit contributes to the total, for Theil T. The table that answers *which* unit drives a movement in the headline series.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `year` | calendar year, 1992–2022 |
| `scope` | unit set — `all` (every unit) |
| `zeros` | pixel zero treatment: `zeros_included` (all land pixels) or `lit_only` (DN > 0). Blank for subnational rows, where the unit is the observation |
| `grouping` | `municipality` |
| `unit` | unit name |
| `pixels` | land pixels in the unit, within scope |
| `mean_dn` | mean DN over those pixels |
| `population_share` | the unit's share of pixels |
| `value_share` | the unit's share of total light |
| `theil_t` | Theil T computed within the unit alone |
| `within_contribution` | the unit's term in the within component: `value_share` × its own `theil_t`. These sum to `within` in the decomposition |

`sha256:645c5ef8bcef32750e3785e52c0586997ba724c3a92da2963e242afeac2401e7`

## San Marino: Theil decomposition

[`SMR/SMR_theil_decomposition.csv`](SMR/SMR_theil_decomposition.csv) — 124 rows

Additive between/within splits of pixel-level Theil. `residual` is the identity check: it stays at machine precision on every defined row, so the split is exact rather than approximate.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `year` | calendar year, 1992–2022 |
| `scope` | unit set — `all` (every unit) |
| `zeros` | pixel zero treatment: `zeros_included` (all land pixels) or `lit_only` (DN > 0). Blank for subnational rows, where the unit is the observation |
| `measure` | `theil_t` or `theil_l` |
| `grouping` | `municipality` only; GADM has no admin-2 layer for this country, so there is no `nested` row |
| `total` | the index over all pixels in scope |
| `between` | between-group component |
| `within` | within-group component |
| `between_share` | `between` ÷ `total` |
| `within_share` | `within` ÷ `total` |
| `between_deleg_within_gov` | the middle term of the nested split: variation between admin-2 units of the same admin-1 unit. `nan` otherwise |
| `residual` | |total − (between + within)|; a correctness check |
| `n_groups` | groups with at least one pixel in scope |

## San Marino: municipality aridity

[`SMR/SMR_adm1_aridity.csv`](SMR/SMR_adm1_aridity.csv) — 9 rows

Climate, measured independently of light. Each unit's share of the five UNEP aridity classes from the Global Aridity Index v3.1, on true cell areas rather than pixel counts. This is what the light-derived exclusion scopes are checked against in [`../docs/aridity.md`](../docs/aridity.md).

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `iso3` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code |
| `gid` | GADM identifier of the municipality |
| `name` | GADM name of the municipality |
| `area_km2` | unit area on the WGS 84 ellipsoid |
| `pixels_total` | aridity cells falling in the unit |
| `pixels_classified` | cells carrying a real aridity value; the rest are ocean or permanent ice, and are excluded from every share below |
| `pixels_unclassified` | `pixels_total` − `pixels_classified` |
| `hyper_arid_share` | area share with aridity index < 0.03 |
| `arid_share` | 0.03 ≤ AI < 0.20 |
| `semi_arid_share` | 0.20 ≤ AI < 0.50 |
| `dry_subhumid_share` | 0.50 ≤ AI < 0.65 |
| `humid_share` | AI ≥ 0.65 |
| `desert_share` | `hyper_arid_share` + `arid_share` — the UNEP definition of desert |
| `dryland_share` | everything below AI 0.65, i.e. 1 − `humid_share` |
| `level` | admin level the row describes; always `adm1` here |

| `dryland_share` | everything below AI 0.65, i.e. 1 − `humid_share` |

## Switzerland: inequality series

[`CHE/CHE_inequality_series.csv`](CHE/CHE_inequality_series.csv) — 124 rows

The headline result. Pixel-level rows are the distribution of DN over land pixels; subnational rows are the distribution of **light density** (SOL/km²) over units, unweighted, so a large unit does not score high merely for being large.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `year` | calendar year, 1992–2022 |
| `level` | `pixel`, `adm1` (canton), `adm2` (district) |
| `level_label` | human-readable form of `level` |
| `scope` | unit set — `all` (every unit) |
| `zeros` | pixel zero treatment: `zeros_included` (all land pixels) or `lit_only` (DN > 0). Blank for subnational rows, where the unit is the observation |
| `n` | observations behind the index: pixels, or units |
| `gini` | Gini coefficient; `nan` if the distribution is all-zero |
| `theil_t` | Theil T = GE(1); maximum is ln(n) |
| `theil_l` | Theil L = GE(0); `nan` whenever any value is 0, since ln(μ/x) diverges — which is why the zeros-included pixel rows are undefined rather than large |
| `sum_of_lights` | total DN over the scope, for reference |
| `lit_share` | fraction of land pixels with DN > 0; pixel rows only |

## Switzerland: Theil decomposition

[`CHE/CHE_theil_decomposition.csv`](CHE/CHE_theil_decomposition.csv) — 372 rows

Additive between/within splits of pixel-level Theil. `residual` is the identity check: it stays at machine precision on every defined row, so the split is exact rather than approximate.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `year` | calendar year, 1992–2022 |
| `scope` | unit set — `all` (every unit) |
| `zeros` | pixel zero treatment: `zeros_included` (all land pixels) or `lit_only` (DN > 0). Blank for subnational rows, where the unit is the observation |
| `measure` | `theil_t` or `theil_l` |
| `grouping` | `canton`, `district`, or `nested` — the three-way pixel → district → canton split |
| `total` | the index over all pixels in scope |
| `between` | between-group component |
| `within` | within-group component |
| `between_share` | `between` ÷ `total` |
| `within_share` | `within` ÷ `total` |
| `between_deleg_within_gov` | the middle term of the nested split: variation between admin-2 units of the same admin-1 unit. `nan` otherwise |
| `residual` | |total − (between + within)|; a correctness check |
| `n_groups` | groups with at least one pixel in scope |

`sha256:f8079e498e7804f9974a468e7816e11d9de71fae4a4dd53f6f503818a341cfe5`

| Column | Meaning |

| `within_contribution` | the unit's term in the within component: `value_share` × its own `theil_t`. These sum to `within` in the decomposition |

## Aridity against darkness, the Arab League pool

[`aridity_vs_light.csv`](aridity_vs_light.csv) — 317 rows

One row per admin-1 unit in this pool, pairing what the climate says with what the light says. ⚠️ **`dark_2022` is not comparable with any other pool's copy of this table**: each cuts at the median `mean_dn_2022` of its own members, and those medians differ. A country in two pools can have a unit dark in one file and lit in the other, correctly.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `iso3` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code |
| `gid` | GADM identifier of the unit |
| `name` | GADM name of the unit |
| `desert_share` | area share that is hyper-arid or arid |
| `dryland_share` | area share below aridity index 0.65 |
| `humid_share` | area share at or above 0.65 |
| `area_km2` | unit area on the WGS 84 ellipsoid |
| `pixels_classified` | aridity cells carrying a real value |
| `mean_dn_1992` | mean DN over the unit's land pixels in 1992 — the zonal tables' `mean_dn`, **not** a density: `density_sol_per_km2` elsewhere in `results/` is that, and the two differ by a few percent on a 1 km grid |
| `mean_dn_2022` | the same for 2022; the column darkness is cut on |
| `majority_arid` | `desert_share` > 0.5 |
| `light_scopes` | the light-derived exclusion scopes this unit belongs to, if any; blank when the light rule never selected it |
| `in_light_scope` | whether `light_scopes` is non-empty |
| `dark_2022` | whether `mean_dn_2022` is strictly below the cross-country median — the cut is a choice, and the set it produces is sensitive to it; Iraq's Ninawa sits exactly on this pool's median, so the strict `<` is load-bearing |
| `cell` | which of the four aridity × darkness cells the unit falls in |

`sha256:e51679e09c99f3e43fa1fa8e34f0397917658bee30a4e76cae48407581f274d1`

## Pace of inequality change, the Arab League pool

[`trends_by_country.csv`](trends_by_country.csv) — 264 rows

Log-linear rates fitted to the published inequality series for this pool's countries. Rates are fitted per country and never pooled, so a country appearing in more than one of these files carries identical numbers in each - only the set of neighbours differs.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `iso3` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code |
| `measure` | `total` (Theil T over all land pixels), `intensive` (Theil T over lit pixels only), `extensive` (share of land pixels lit), `between_share` (share of Theil T lying between admin-1 units) |
| `measure_note` | the same, spelled out |
| `window` | `full` 1992–2022, `dmsp` 1992–2013, `viirs` 2014–2022; the two eras are not comparable to each other |
| `first_year` | first year with a usable value in the window |
| `last_year` | last such year |
| `n_years` | usable observations behind the fit |
| `percent_per_year` | the fitted slope of ln(value) against year, as a percentage |
| `r_squared` | goodness of the straight-line fit; `nan` for a series with no variation at all, which has no slope to explain |
| `half_life_years` | ln(2) ÷ |rate| — years to halve; `nan` for a series that is not falling, because a rising series has no half-life |
| `direction` | `falling`, `rising`, `flat` or `undefined` |
| `monotone` | whether `r_squared` clears the threshold; `False` means one slope does not describe the series and the rate is a direction, not a pace |
| `trajectory` | the country's typology label, assigned by rule |
| `trajectory_reason` | which rule assigned it, in one clause |

`sha256:e2cd13d5b3ff51d66acbbe6927f7b1b8437203ffd2e4efcb5bb388e684fe0af2`

## Aridity against darkness, the North America pool

[`north-america_aridity_vs_light.csv`](north-america_aridity_vs_light.csv) — 379 rows

One row per admin-1 unit in this pool, pairing what the climate says with what the light says. ⚠️ **`dark_2022` is not comparable with any other pool's copy of this table**: each cuts at the median `mean_dn_2022` of its own members, and those medians differ. A country in two pools can have a unit dark in one file and lit in the other, correctly.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `iso3` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code |
| `gid` | GADM identifier of the unit |
| `name` | GADM name of the unit |
| `desert_share` | area share that is hyper-arid or arid |
| `dryland_share` | area share below aridity index 0.65 |
| `humid_share` | area share at or above 0.65 |
| `area_km2` | unit area on the WGS 84 ellipsoid |
| `pixels_classified` | aridity cells carrying a real value |
| `mean_dn_1992` | mean DN over the unit's land pixels in 1992 — the zonal tables' `mean_dn`, **not** a density: `density_sol_per_km2` elsewhere in `results/` is that, and the two differ by a few percent on a 1 km grid |

| `dark_2022` | whether `mean_dn_2022` is strictly below the cross-country median — the cut is a choice, and the set it produces is sensitive to it; Washington State sits exactly on this pool's median, so the strict `<` is load-bearing |
| `cell` | which of the four aridity × darkness cells the unit falls in |

## Morocco: clipped rasters

`MAR/raster/` — 31 files, 5.2 MB

The 31 annual LRCC-DVNL grids cut to Morocco at 1 km, `EPSG:8857`, nodata 127, LZW. Pixels outside the GADM national boundary are masked, not merely cropped, so a neighbour's light does not leak into a bounding box. Every number in this country's tables is computed from exactly these files.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.
* **Geotransforms are not identical across years.** They differ by fractions of a millimetre, inherited from the published rasters. Same pixel grid for every practical purpose, but an exact-equality check on the transform will reject the stack; compare with a tolerance.
* These carry a real `EPSG:8857`, unlike the published files, whose `LOCAL_CS` declaration needs `satimg raster fix-crs`.

## Palestine: clipped rasters

The 31 annual LRCC-DVNL grids cut to Palestine at 1 km, `EPSG:8857`, nodata 127, LZW. Pixels outside the GADM national boundary are masked, not merely cropped, so a neighbour's light does not leak into a bounding box. Every number in this country's tables is computed from exactly these files.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.
* **Geotransforms are not identical across years.** They differ by fractions of a millimetre, inherited from the published rasters. Same pixel grid for every practical purpose, but an exact-equality check on the transform will reject the stack; compare with a tolerance.

## Angola: clipped rasters

`AGO/raster/` — 31 files, 4.8 MB

The 31 annual LRCC-DVNL grids cut to Angola at 1 km, `EPSG:8857`, nodata 127, LZW. Pixels outside the GADM national boundary are masked, not merely cropped, so a neighbour's light does not leak into a bounding box. Every number in this country's tables is computed from exactly these files.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.
* **Geotransforms are not identical across years.** They differ by fractions of a millimetre, inherited from the published rasters. Same pixel grid for every practical purpose, but an exact-equality check on the transform will reject the stack; compare with a tolerance.
* These carry a real `EPSG:8857`, unlike the published files, whose `LOCAL_CS` declaration needs `satimg raster fix-crs`.

## Central African Republic: clipped rasters

`CAF/raster/` — 31 files, 2.8 MB

The 31 annual LRCC-DVNL grids cut to Central African Republic at 1 km, `EPSG:8857`, nodata 127, LZW. Pixels outside the GADM national boundary are masked, not merely cropped, so a neighbour's light does not leak into a bounding box. Every number in this country's tables is computed from exactly these files.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.
* **Geotransforms are not identical across years.** They differ by fractions of a millimetre, inherited from the published rasters. Same pixel grid for every practical purpose, but an exact-equality check on the transform will reject the stack; compare with a tolerance.
* These carry a real `EPSG:8857`, unlike the published files, whose `LOCAL_CS` declaration needs `satimg raster fix-crs`.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.
* **Geotransforms are not identical across years.** They differ by fractions of a millimetre, inherited from the published rasters. Same pixel grid for every practical purpose, but an exact-equality check on the transform will reject the stack; compare with a tolerance.
* These carry a real `EPSG:8857`, unlike the published files, whose `LOCAL_CS` declaration needs `satimg raster fix-crs`.

## Zimbabwe: clipped rasters

`ZWE/raster/` — 31 files, 1.8 MB

The 31 annual LRCC-DVNL grids cut to Zimbabwe at 1 km, `EPSG:8857`, nodata 127, LZW. Pixels outside the GADM national boundary are masked, not merely cropped, so a neighbour's light does not leak into a bounding box. Every number in this country's tables is computed from exactly these files.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.
* **Geotransforms are not identical across years.** They differ by fractions of a millimetre, inherited from the published rasters. Same pixel grid for every practical purpose, but an exact-equality check on the transform will reject the stack; compare with a tolerance.
* These carry a real `EPSG:8857`, unlike the published files, whose `LOCAL_CS` declaration needs `satimg raster fix-crs`.

## Costa Rica: clipped rasters

`CRI/raster/` — 31 files, 1.6 MB

The 31 annual LRCC-DVNL grids cut to Costa Rica at 1 km, `EPSG:8857`, nodata 127, LZW. Pixels outside the GADM national boundary are masked, not merely cropped, so a neighbour's light does not leak into a bounding box. Every number in this country's tables is computed from exactly these files.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.
* **Geotransforms are not identical across years.** They differ by fractions of a millimetre, inherited from the published rasters. Same pixel grid for every practical purpose, but an exact-equality check on the transform will reject the stack; compare with a tolerance.
* These carry a real `EPSG:8857`, unlike the published files, whose `LOCAL_CS` declaration needs `satimg raster fix-crs`.

## Panama: clipped rasters

`PAN/raster/` — 31 files, 1.0 MB

The 31 annual LRCC-DVNL grids cut to Panama at 1 km, `EPSG:8857`, nodata 127, LZW. Pixels outside the GADM national boundary are masked, not merely cropped, so a neighbour's light does not leak into a bounding box. Every number in this country's tables is computed from exactly these files.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.
* **Geotransforms are not identical across years.** They differ by fractions of a millimetre, inherited from the published rasters. Same pixel grid for every practical purpose, but an exact-equality check on the transform will reject the stack; compare with a tolerance.
* These carry a real `EPSG:8857`, unlike the published files, whose `LOCAL_CS` declaration needs `satimg raster fix-crs`.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.
* **Geotransforms are not identical across years.** They differ by fractions of a millimetre, inherited from the published rasters. Same pixel grid for every practical purpose, but an exact-equality check on the transform will reject the stack; compare with a tolerance.
* These carry a real `EPSG:8857`, unlike the published files, whose `LOCAL_CS` declaration needs `satimg raster fix-crs`.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.

## Luxembourg: clipped rasters

The 31 annual LRCC-DVNL grids cut to Luxembourg at 1 km, `EPSG:8857`, nodata 127, LZW. Pixels outside the GADM national boundary are masked, not merely cropped, so a neighbour's light does not leak into a bounding box. Every number in this country's tables is computed from exactly these files.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.

## North Macedonia: clipped rasters

`MKD/raster/` — 31 files, 492.0 KB

The 31 annual LRCC-DVNL grids cut to North Macedonia at 1 km, `EPSG:8857`, nodata 127, LZW. Pixels outside the GADM national boundary are masked, not merely cropped, so a neighbour's light does not leak into a bounding box. Every number in this country's tables is computed from exactly these files.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.
* **Geotransforms are not identical across years.** They differ by fractions of a millimetre, inherited from the published rasters. Same pixel grid for every practical purpose, but an exact-equality check on the transform will reject the stack; compare with a tolerance.
* These carry a real `EPSG:8857`, unlike the published files, whose `LOCAL_CS` declaration needs `satimg raster fix-crs`.

## Slovakia: clipped rasters

`SVK/raster/` — 31 files, 1.2 MB

The 31 annual LRCC-DVNL grids cut to Slovakia at 1 km, `EPSG:8857`, nodata 127, LZW. Pixels outside the GADM national boundary are masked, not merely cropped, so a neighbour's light does not leak into a bounding box. Every number in this country's tables is computed from exactly these files.

* **The series is not dtype-homogeneous.** 1992 is `int8`, 1993–2013 `int16`, and 2014–2022 `float32` carrying *fractional* DN. Reading the stack with one fixed dtype silently truncates the VIIRS era — a downward bias in exactly the half of the series where lit area grows fastest.
* **Geotransforms are not identical across years.** They differ by fractions of a millimetre, inherited from the published rasters. Same pixel grid for every practical purpose, but an exact-equality check on the transform will reject the stack; compare with a tolerance.
* These carry a real `EPSG:8857`, unlike the published files, whose `LOCAL_CS` declaration needs `satimg raster fix-crs`.
